name: DocuSign
summary: DocuSign requires users to create their own OAuth 2.0 Integration Key for API authentication; Composio does not offer a managed OAuth flow, so you must configure your own credentials in the DocuSign Admin panel and wire them to Composio using the provided redirect URI.
decision: You must set up your own OAuth app (Integration Key) within the DocuSign Admin panel and connect it to Composio, as Composio-managed authentication is not available for DocuSign.

prerequisites.title: DocuSign Developer Account
prerequisites.body: You must have a DocuSign developer account, which can be created for free at developers.docusign.com.

steps.title: Open DocuSign Admin Panel
steps.body: Sign in to your DocuSign account at app.docusign.com and navigate to the Admin section using the top navigation bar (Admin role required).
steps.note: If you do not have Admin privileges, contact your DocuSign account owner.

steps.title: Navigate to Apps and Keys
steps.body: In the Admin panel sidebar, scroll to INTEGRATIONS and select 'Apps and Keys'.

steps.title: Add App and Integration Key
steps.body: Click 'Add App and Integration Key', enter a clear, descriptive app name (e.g. composio-docusign-connector), and confirm the creation.
steps.note: This name is visible to users on the consent screen.

steps.title: Copy the Integration Key
steps.body: On the app details page, copy the Integration Key (Client ID) from the General Info section.

steps.title: Set Authentication to User Application
steps.body: Under Authentication, for User Application, select 'Yes' to indicate your app is confidential (can store client secret securely) and enable Authorization Code Grant.
steps.note: PKCE is optional for the basic flow.

steps.title: Generate and Save Secret Key
steps.body: Click '+ Add Secret Key' to generate a client secret. Copy and save it securely as you will not be able to see it again.

steps.title: Create Auth Config in Composio
steps.body: In Composio, create a DocuSign Auth Config using the Client ID and Secret Key generated above, with the specified redirect URI.

steps.title: Connect User Account
steps.body: Connect a DocuSign user account to Composio and complete the OAuth user consent in your browser.
steps.note: The cited page adds a condition this claim omits: > Before you start: Make sure you have a DocuSign developer account (free at developers.docusign.com), access to your Composio project, and a browser available to complete the OAuth consent flow.

blockers.title: Missing Admin Privileges
blockers.body: You must have DocuSign Admin rights to access Apps and Keys and set up integration.

human_actions.title: Log into DocuSign with Admin Rights
human_actions.body: A person must log into their DocuSign account and confirm they have Admin permissions.

human_actions.title: Create App and Integration Key
human_actions.body: A person needs to create a new Integration Key in the DocuSign Admin panel under Apps and Keys.

human_actions.title: Configure OAuth Settings
human_actions.body: A human must configure authentication as a User Application, generate and securely copy both the Integration Key and Secret Key, and add the exact Composio redirect URI.

human_actions.title: Input Credentials in Composio
human_actions.body: A person must enter these credentials in Composio when creating the DocuSign Auth Config.

human_actions.title: Approve OAuth Consent Screen
human_actions.body: A human must authorize the Composio app with their DocuSign account through the OAuth web flow.
